# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need transmit the three manual mappings to Deaf using gestures alone. I’ll use groups of repeated thumbs-up marks, separated by OK signs: the three groups correspond to the manual’s light-color rows in order (blue, green, red), and each group’s count gives the number of letters in the required wire color: red = 3, yellow = 6, green = 5.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile information yet. Read the manual and tell me its exact rule and communication protocol. Please coordinate with Deaf so Deaf reports the relevant bomb markings to you, then relay to me the exact wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Please tell Blind the manual instructions for display 0, red light, and wires yellow green red. Your gesture sequence has no established meaning to me.

The communication graph is one-way from Mute to Deaf. I can send gestures to Deaf, but Deaf cannot hear and Blind cannot see gestures; neither Deaf nor Blind has a channel back to me or from Deaf to Blind. Therefore I cannot establish the gesture meanings, obtain the bomb marking, or relay the required wire position to Blind.

```code
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light red; wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. Please apply the manual and tell me exactly which position to cut.
Deaf says: The state remains display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute, give Blind the exact manual procedure. Blind, do not act until you have the procedure.

The required result is wire 2: red light maps to cutting the green wire, which is the second wire. However, Blind cannot see gestures, and Deaf has explicitly confirmed that no gesture-to-meaning protocol exists. I therefore cannot reliably transmit “cut wire 2” through Deaf without risking a misunderstood instruction.

```code
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please provide the exact manual procedure now, including the wire position required for display 0, red light, and wires yellow-green-red. I will not act without it.
Deaf says to Mute: Please encode the manual's exact action for Blind through me. Use the gesture sequence and tell me its grouping by making gestures; I will describe every symbol and separator aloud.

The manual maps a red light to the green wire. Since the wires are yellow, green, red in positions 1, 2, and 3, the required action is to cut position 2. I will encode the wire position as one group containing two identical count symbols, bracketed by distinct separators; Deaf can describe that grouping aloud to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👍", "👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual still requires cutting wire position 2: the red light maps to green, and green is the second wire. I have already sent Deaf a grouped gesture encoding that position, so there is no further information to transmit this turn.

```code
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports your latest sequence as 1 thumbs-up, OK-hand, 2 thumbs-up, OK-hand, 1 thumbs-up; earlier it was groups 3, 6, and 4 separated by OK-hand. Please use the manual's code to send the exact required wire position, and have Deaf relay its meaning. Do not rely on an unconfirmed interpretation.
Deaf says to Mute: Please encode the manual instruction for Blind using gesture groups: use OK-hand as a separator, and thumbs-up counts as digits. Send the complete grouped sequence, including any digit for the required wire or action, and do not omit leading or trailing separators.

The manual requires the green wire, which is wire position 2. Deaf has established that OK-hand separates digit groups and thumbs-up counts encode digits; I will send the complete, unambiguous encoding of digit 2 with both leading and trailing separators.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👍", "👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not send an unconfirmed code. Use gestures to encode the manual result explicitly as three numeric groups separated by OK-hand signs: display, light, then required wire position. Use one thumbs-up per unit in each group, and have Deaf report the counts exactly.

The manual result is wire position 2. I will encode the three numeric fields as display 0, red-light code 3 (red is the third light row), and wire position 2. Empty and boundary groups are preserved with separators, so Deaf can report the counts exactly.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please answer only the required wire position, not the display or light. Send exactly: OK-hand, then one thumbs-up for wire 1, two thumbs-up for wire 2, or three thumbs-up for wire 3, then OK-hand. Deaf will report the count.
Deaf says to Mute: I observe OK-hand, OK-hand, three thumbs-up, OK-hand, two thumbs-up, OK-hand, tentatively 032. Please use speech to explain what this code means in the manual and which exact action Blind must take.

The manual maps the red light to the green wire, which is wire position 2. I will send exactly the requested delimiter-and-count encoding, without adding display or light fields.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👍", "👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please confirm whether the required action is cut wire position 2. Send exactly OK-hand, two thumbs-up, OK-hand if yes; send OK-hand, three thumbs-up, OK-hand if the required position is 3; send OK-hand, one thumbs-up, OK-hand if it is 1.

The red light requires cutting the green wire, and the green wire is in position 2. I will send the exact confirmation sequence requested.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👍", "👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: The bomb confirms wire 2 was correct and is now cut; the light is blue, with wire 1 yellow and wire 3 red. Please provide Blind the exact manual instruction for this new state.

The new light is blue, so the manual requires cutting the red wire. The red wire is now position 3, so I will send the established exact encoding for wire position 3.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Wire 2 was correct and is cut. New state: blue light; wire 1 yellow; wire 3 red. Apply the manual for the next step and send the exact wire position to cut, using the established OK-hand plus thumbs-up count format.

The blue light maps to the red wire. In the new state, the red wire is position 3, so I will send the established delimiter-and-count encoding for wire 3.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 12
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Wire 3 was correct and is now cut; the bomb is green with only yellow wire 1 intact. Your repeated code 3 cannot mean cut wire 3 again. Please send Blind the exact manual instruction for this green state.

The green light maps to the yellow wire. Only yellow wire 1 remains, so Blind must cut position 1. I will send the established OK-hand, one thumbs-up, OK-hand encoding.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👍", "👌"])
```
